title: Digital Agency Islamabad: AI, Tech, Marketing | 22 Signals
description: 22 Signals works with organisations in Islamabad on AI, cloud, data, websites, apps, SEO, ads and video, with one accountable lead and London head office.
h1: Digital agency for Islamabad: we work with organisations across the capital
intro: 22 Signals is a business solutions company working with organisations in Islamabad and Rawalpindi. We build the systems you run on, from AI, cloud and data to websites and apps, then grow them with SEO, paid media and video. One accountable lead, specialist teams behind them, and every date in writing.

sections.h: Who we work with in Islamabad
p: We work with established organisations in Islamabad, usually with between five and 500 staff: companies that sell to government and development partners, software and IT exporters, telecom suppliers, private hospitals and clinics, universities and school groups, and property developers. We also work with founders, including those coming through the National Incubation Center, when the fit is right.

What they share is a habit of being checked. Islamabad buyers answer to auditors, donors, boards or overseas clients, so they need a partner who documents decisions, sticks to agreed dates and can explain every line of a proposal. That suits how we already work. If you searched for 'digital agency Islamabad' because you need a partner who can stand up to an audit, that is the gap we fill.

sections.h: What the capital's economy asks of a partner
p: Islamabad is not a smaller Lahore or Karachi. Its economy is shaped by the federal government, regulators and the organisations around them, and that changes what good technology and marketing work looks like here.
list: Government, regulators and their suppliers, where work is often bought through tenders on e-PADS, the federal electronic procurement system
International organisations, embassies and NGOs, with donor rules on data, branding and reporting
Telecoms: PTA is headquartered in Islamabad, and so are several of the country's mobile operators
The IT and software export sector, supported by the Pakistan Software Export Board, which is also based in the capital
Startups around the National Incubation Center, backed by Ignite and the Ministry of IT and Telecommunication
Education and healthcare, from large universities to private hospitals and diagnostic chains
Real estate, from Blue Area offices and F-sector markets to newer communities such as Gulberg Greens

p: If you came here looking for a digital agency: Islamabad clients usually need far more than marketing, so we cover the technology as well. Each service has its own Islamabad page with the detail, examples and FAQs. In short:
list: AI consultancy: finding where AI pays off, with governance your auditors and donors accept
AI automation: taking repetitive admin off desks, with WhatsApp, email, CRM and spreadsheets connected
Business intelligence and data analytics: one version of the numbers, in Power BI, Looker Studio or Tableau
Cloud consulting: AWS, Azure or Google Cloud, designed around the Cloud First Policy's data classes
Web development: bilingual English and Urdu sites, portals and redesigns that keep rankings
App development: iOS, Android and web apps with wallet, Raast and card payments
SEO and GEO: ranking for sector and markaz searches and showing up in answers from ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Paid media: Google, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok ads tracked through to WhatsApp and calls
Video production, animation and AI video: explainers, brand films, reels and live broadcast
3D rendering: property, interior and product visuals that match approved plans

p: Pakistan's Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 is the main law on unauthorised access to data and systems, and it shapes how we set up access, logging and security for every client. The Personal Data Protection Bill has been drafted by the Ministry of IT and Telecommunication and is still not law, so we build as though consent, retention and transfer rules will apply. Public sector work follows the federal Cloud First Policy, and telecom-related work sits under PTA. Firms regulated by the SECP, which is also headquartered in Islamabad, bring their own requirements.
We are not a law firm. We design systems so the compliance questions have clear answers, and we work alongside your legal team for sign-off.

Much of the work in Islamabad is bought formally: expressions of interest, requests for proposals, tenders, donor procurement and vendor registration. We respond with a clear scope, named deliverables, a timeline and a separate commercial section where the process requires it. If a tender asks for a registration or document we cannot provide, we say so before you spend time evaluating us.

Our head office is in London, and we work with Islamabad organisations remotely. We do not have an office in Islamabad. Pakistan Standard Time is five hours ahead of London in winter and four in summer, so a 10:00 London call is 15:00 PKT from late October to late March and 14:00 PKT the rest of the year. Most clients choose a fixed weekly slot in the Islamabad afternoon.

Quick questions run on WhatsApp, which is how most Pakistani teams prefer to talk, and every decision is confirmed in writing. We work in English and Urdu. When a workshop, site visit or shoot needs people in the same room, we come to Islamabad when the project needs it, agreed in advance.

When they hire a digital agency, Islamabad organisations often end up juggling it alongside a web developer, an IT vendor and a freelancer for video. We cover AI, cloud and data, marketing, and video, animation and 3D in one team, led by one accountable Signal Lead. Projects run through Talk, Plan, Build and Grow, and every date agreed goes in writing.

We have worked with more than 30 companies across four regions: the United States, the United Kingdom, the UAE and Pakistan. If you want to see whether we fit, book a 15-minute call; it is a fit check, not a pitch.

sections.h: Islamabad, Rawalpindi and the rest of Pakistan
p: For most clients, Islamabad and Rawalpindi are one market, with staff and customers crossing the Faizabad Interchange every day. Our pages for the capital cover both. If you operate across the country, see our Pakistan page and our pages for Lahore and Karachi, where buyers, industries and search behaviour differ again.

faqs.q: Does 22 Signals have an office in Islamabad?
faqs.a: No. Our head office is in London, and we work with Islamabad and Rawalpindi organisations remotely, with meetings in the Islamabad afternoon so both sides are at their desks. When a project genuinely needs us in the room, for a workshop, a site visit or a shoot, we plan a visit when the project needs it.

faqs.q: What kind of Islamabad organisations do you work with?
faqs.a: Mostly established organisations with five to 500 staff: government and donor suppliers, software exporters, telecom suppliers, hospitals and clinics, universities and schools, and property developers. We also take on founders when the project fits, including startups from the National Incubation Center.

faqs.q: Can you bid on government or donor tenders?
faqs.a: Often, yes. We write technical proposals with scope, deliverables, timeline and a separate commercial section. Some tenders require local registration, tax status or other documents, and some donors set eligibility rules. We check those first and tell you plainly if we cannot take part.

Yes. We can hold meetings in English or Urdu, and we build Urdu websites, Urdu and Roman Urdu content, Urdu voiceovers and AI tools that read and reply in Urdu. Every piece of Urdu content is checked by a person who reads it fluently before it goes out.

faqs.q: How do you handle data protection in Pakistan?
faqs.a: We design around PECA 2016, the Cloud First Policy for public sector data, and the direction of the draft Personal Data Protection Bill. In practice that means named access, logs, data kept only as long as needed, and clear records of where data is stored. Your legal team gives the final sign-off.

Get in touch through the site. In a short first conversation we ask about the problem, your timeline and who needs to approve the work, then tell you honestly whether we are a fit. If we are, the next step is a written plan with scope, dates and the people involved on both sides.
